s: A payments company is building a balance service on Amazon DynamoDB. The service must accept writes in multiple AWS Regions and must keep operating if any single Region becomes unavailable. Any read in any Region must return the most recently committed balance, and a Regional failure must not lose any acknowledged write (RPO of zero). The company accepts higher write latency to get these guarantees. Which solution meets these requirements?
o: Create a DynamoDB global table configured for multi-Region strong consistency, using three Regions or two replica Regions plus a witness Region, and issue strongly consistent reads.
Create a DynamoDB global table with the default multi-Region eventual consistency mode and issue strongly consistent reads in each Region.
Use DynamoDB Streams and AWS Lambda functions to replicate writes synchronously to tables in two other Regions before returning success to the caller.
Use Aurora PostgreSQL global database with write forwarding enabled on the secondary clusters, and set the session consistency to GLOBAL.

w.y: With multi-Region strong consistency, global tables replicate writes synchronously, so a strongly consistent read in any Region returns the latest value. This gives an RPO of zero, at the price of higher write latency, which the company explicitly accepts.

o.A: Correct: MRSC global tables are the built-in option for an RPO of zero and globally strongly consistent reads.
o.B: In eventual mode, a strongly consistent read is only Region-local. Asynchronous replication with last-writer-wins can lose writes in a Regional failure.
o.C: DynamoDB Streams is asynchronous, so a Lambda function cannot make the original write synchronous. This is fragile custom code.
o.D: Write forwarding still sends writes to one primary Region, and a Regional failover can lose writes that have not replicated yet.

d: RPO of zero; latest value in any Region
